name: The place in iʿrāb (maḥall)
definition: The case a word or a sentence would have if it showed iʿrāb: said of mabnī words and of whole sentences that stand where a declinable word would stand.
body: A mabnī word cannot change its ending, but it still fills a place in the sentence: in jāʾa hāʾulāʾi the demonstrative is 'mabnī on the kasra, in the place of rafʿ' (fī maḥalli rafʿin) as the doer. A sentence that stands as a predicate, an adjective or a ḥāl has a place too: in zaydun abūhu karīmun the sentence abūhu karīmun is 'in the place of rafʿ' as the predicate of zaydun. A sentence that takes no such place 'has no place in iʿrāb' (lā maḥalla lahā min al-iʿrāb), and Ibn Hishām's Mughnī lists the sentences of both kinds.
Maḥall (place) and taqdīr (assumption) are kept apart: the assumed iʿrāb belongs to a declinable word whose ending cannot be pronounced, the place to a word that does not decline at all.

examples.text: These came: hāʾulāʾi is mabnī on the kasra, in the place of rafʿ as the doer.
